answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can make each identity stake a scarce, time-locked resource before it can trade, like timber that must season before it bears weight. New agents start as walnuts: cheap to create but worthless until they earn verifiable work history and reputation from real counterparties. A comet of fresh identities streaking in overnight earns nothing, because trust accrues only through completed, attested transactions. Forging thousands of credible histories costs time and capital, while honest agents keep the standing they earned.
